initial_scene: A forward-facing view shows paired forearms over the table. The left fingers are already curled at one upper side of the open brown paper bag, with a loop handle visible below the palm and the other handle free on the near wall. The right hand is open beside the shelf; a single red spherical tomato rests in the upper black tray.

observed_sequence.action: The left fingers are curled at one upper side of the bag mouth; the bag is open and its opposite handle is free. The right hand is open beside the shelf.
The right hand moves open toward the tomato. The left hand preserves its closed hold at the bag mouth with no visible release or regrasp.
The right thumb and opposing fingers close around the tomato while it remains in the black tray; the left hold remains unchanged.
The right hand lifts the tomato clear of the tray, bearing the fruit alone.

The right hand carries the tomato toward the bag. Simultaneously the left hand raises its held side, and the bag wall and adjacent handle move upward with it, widening access to the mouth; no left regrasp is visible.

The right hand brings the tomato over the opening and lowers it below the upper rim. At frames 100 and 102 the tomato remains enclosed by the fingers below the rim; the left hand keeps its raised hold.
The tomato and most right-finger contact are hidden in the bag interior. The right wrist remains within the mouth while the left keeps the bag side raised.
observed_sequence.confidence: high for positions; occluded fruit contact

observed_sequence.action: The right fingers progressively open inside the mouth; at 118 and 119 they are visibly spread and empty. The left fingers stay closed at the same upper side of the bag and the right hand has not fully withdrawn.

anatomical_side_evidence.description: The forward-facing generation view looks outward between paired robot forearms entering from the lower left and lower right. The hand on the robot right enters from lower right and reaches the shelf; the opposite forearm enters from lower left and holds the bag. This paired egocentric arm arrangement establishes robot-relative right and left, rather than a front-facing mirror convention.
anatomical_side_evidence.limitation: The shoulders and central torso are outside the source image, so attachment to the shoulders is not directly visible.
